newsitem.title: USA: U.S. government can resume immigrant deportations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. government can resume immigrant deportations.

text.p: The U.S. government is free to begin deportations of immigrants after a federal judge on Thursday was unable to reach a decision on a preliminary injunction blocking any such action.

U.S. District Judge James Lawrence King said he hoped that immigration officials would use their discretion and not immediately begin deportations when a temporary restraining order expires at midnight.
King said, however, that the decision was the government's.

After listening to hours of lawyers' arguments Thursday, King said he had far too much material to absorb to make a hasty decision on issuing a preliminary injunction against deportations. The injunction was sought by lawyers in a class-action suit on behalf of some 40,000 Nicaraguans and other immigrants.
New immigration laws enacted in April have left tens of thousands of immigrants, many of whom have lived in the United States legally for years, open to deportation to their home countries.
After the decision was announced, hundreds of Nicaraguans gathered outside the courthouse shouted in dismay and cried "Justice, Justice."
